requirements.md AC-010 states 'no other condition produces a non-zero exit' beyond the sixteen REQ-002 diagnostic-id rows, but AC-013 (two rows below, same table) states the exit-code contract includes '2 on a CLI usage error (AC-001)'. A CLI usage error is explicitly not a REQ-002 Block (Field Definitions ties 'Block' strictly to REQ-002's own taxonomy, and AC-001's missing-required-flag fixtures are a distinct usage-error path), yet AC-013 confirms it produces a non-zero exit (2) -- directly negating AC-010's literal claim. Downstream failure mode: a design reviewer or future test author relying on requirements.md's own AC-010 wording (rather than acceptance-tests.md's cleaner TEST-010 description, which does not repeat this phrase) could misread the Block table as an exhaustive enumeration of every non-zero-exit condition, producing an incorrect implementation or a spurious 'no other non-zero exit' assertion inside the block test suite that conflicts with AC-001's own exit-2 fixtures. This is a one-line acceptance-criteria wording defect fixable before design/task work, squarely spec review's own scope, not implementation review's. Severity is Major rather than Critical because AC-013's own adjacent, unambiguous text and acceptance-tests.md's clean TEST-010 wording limit the practical blast radius -- it does not create a safety or workflow-boundary conflict or render the specification unreviewable.
